title: Nasdaq Plummets 350 Points as Google Shares Dive: Live Market Updates from WSJ
body:
The Nasdaq Composite plunged more than 350 points on Tuesday, dragging the technology‑heavy index into a steep intraday decline and sparking fresh worries about the health of the broader market. At the center of the sell‑off was Alphabet Inc., whose shares tumbled to their lowest level in the company’s history after the earnings report failed to meet expectations. The rout erased roughly $500 billion in market value from the Google parent in a single session, marking the most severe one‑day loss for the stock in its 25‑year history.

The slide came as investors digested Alphabet’s fourth‑quarter results, which revealed a 12 % slowdown in revenue growth and a modest miss on earnings per share. While the company posted $86 billion in revenue, analysts had been looking for a figure closer to $89 billion, and the earnings beat was limited to a few cents. More concerning to the market was the company’s guidance for the upcoming quarter, which suggested a further deceleration in ad spending and a slower rollout of its AI‑driven products. The disappointing outlook prompted a wave of profit‑taking across the tech sector, with Apple, Microsoft and Meta also slipping, though none as sharply as Alphabet.

The broader market reaction was swift. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.6 %, while the S&P 500 fell 0.9 %, underscoring how heavily weighted the indices are on big‑tech performance. Bond yields rose modestly as investors sought safety, and the US Dollar Index edged higher, reflecting a risk‑off sentiment that extended beyond equities. Market commentators noted that the decline came after a period of relative calm, during which the Nasdaq had rallied on hopes that artificial‑intelligence breakthroughs would sustain growth for the sector. The current correction, they said, may be a “re‑pricing” of those expectations, especially as advertisers remain cautious amid a lingering economic slowdown.

Analysts also highlighted that Alphabet’s troubles are not isolated to its core advertising business. The company’s ambitious bets on generative AI, cloud services and hardware have yet to translate into the kind of revenue acceleration investors hoped for. While its AI‑driven search enhancements and the launch of new enterprise tools have generated buzz, the monetization timeline remains uncertain. Moreover, heightened regulatory scrutiny in the United States and Europe adds another layer of risk, potentially curbing the firm’s ability to leverage its data assets. The combination of slower ad spend, execution risk on new ventures, and a tougher macro environment created a perfect storm that rattled confidence in the stock.

Despite the sharp drop, some investors see a silver lining. The price correction has brought Alphabet’s valuation closer to historical averages, potentially setting the stage for a buying opportunity if the company can demonstrate tangible progress on its AI roadmap and stabilize ad revenue. Wall Street strategists suggest that a rebound could be on the horizon, provided the firm delivers clearer guidance and the broader economy shows signs of resilience. In the meantime, the market is likely to remain volatile, with traders watching closely for any fresh data on consumer spending, corporate earnings and central‑bank policy that could sway sentiment.

Looking ahead, the Nasdaq’s near‑term trajectory will depend on whether the tech sector can regain momentum after the earnings shock. Investors will be monitoring upcoming reports from other heavyweight names, as well as macro indicators such as inflation trends and employment figures, to gauge the depth of the risk‑off mood. If Alphabet can turn its AI initiatives into revenue‑generating products and restore confidence in its growth outlook, the index may recover its footing. Conversely, continued weakness in advertising spend or further regulatory setbacks could keep pressure on the Nasdaq and prolong the market’s uneasy pause.
